WPA Weekly News - Friday
4th September 2026
textBlocks:
Welcome to this week’s school
newsletter!

A very warm welcome back to all of
our pupils and families after what
has been a very hot summer break. It
has been wonderful to see the
children return to school with smiling
faces, ready for another exciting year
of learning and growth.

Over the past two days, the children
have been settling into their new
classrooms, getting to know their
teachers, reconnecting with friends
and beginning to establish new
routines. We have been incredibly
proud of how positively they have
approached the start of the new
school year.

We would also like to extend a huge
welcome to our new Reception
children and their families. The
children have done amazingly well at
settling into school life, exploring
their new environment and beginning
to build relationships with their
classmates and staff. We are so
pleased with how confidently they
have embraced this important
milestone.

This year, our school newsletter will
be shared every Friday afternoon,
keeping families up to date with
school events, celebrations and
important information. As we have
only been back for two days, this
week's newsletter is a brief one.
However, please do take a look ahead
at the year to come with the attached
term dates. These will be included
and updated weekly throughout the
year to help you stay informed of key
dates and events.

We look forward to another fantastic
year working together and thank you
for your continued support.

Please review the list of upcoming
events below. Dates marked in green
represent newly added entries for
your calendar.

A quick reminder that our PTFA sell
high‑quality

It’s a great way to save money,
support the school, and give uniform
items a new life.

Please check out their page if you
need any extra bits for the term

If you require any further
information or have any questions or
concerns, please don’t hesitate to get
in touch with us in the school office -
we’re here to help.

Want to learn more? Take a look
around our website at

— you’ll find
plenty of helpful information.

REMEMBER - If you feel that a child
is unsafe, then please use the
following ways to contact help.

Call Social Services on 0345 045 5203
and make a referral. This can be an
anonymous referral if this feels safer.

Call 999 IF CHILD IS IN
IMMEDIATE DANGER.

You can also use our emergency email
address
(safeguarding@wpa.education). BUT
please use the other options first, so
as not to delay help for a child.

WPA Weekly News - Friday
11th September 2026
textBlocks:
Welcome to this week’s school
newsletter!

It has been wonderful to complete our
first full week back at school and to
see how positively all of the children
have settled into their new
classrooms. The children have
continued to build new friendships,
establish routines, and get to know
their teachers, and we are incredibly
proud of how well they have embraced
the start of the new academic year.

Our Reception children have enjoyed
staying for lunch with us this week
and are settling in beautifully. It has
been lovely to see their confidence
grow each day as they become
familiar with school life and all the
exciting opportunities that lie ahead.

We have also been delighted to
welcome so many parents and carers
into school this week for our Meet the
Teacher events. These sessions have
been very well attended, and we hope
they have provided a valuable
opportunity for you to get to know
your child's class teacher, learn more
about classroom routines, and gain
an insight into the exciting learning
planned for the year ahead.

Thank you for your continued
support. We look forward to another
fantastic week of learning,
achievement, and enjoyment across
the school. Have a lovely weekend!

Please review the list of upcoming
events below. Dates marked in green
represent newly added entries for
your calendar.

If your child requires an inhaler
whilst at school, please ensure that it
is brought to the school office as soon
as possible. To help us keep our
records accurate and ensure we can
safely administer medication when
needed, parents and carers are also
asked to complete an updated
Medication Administration Form.
Having an in-date inhaler and
current medical information available
is essential for keeping all children
safe and well during the school day.

If you have any questions, please
contact the school office who will be
happy to help.

Thank you for your cooperation in

At our school, we are proud to
support our Young Carers and
recognise the important role they
play within their families. We work
closely with Centre 33 to provide
external support, while internally we
offer fortnightly Young Carers

ensure our Young Carers feel valued,
understood, and supported. We are
also committed to raising awareness

school day. We recognise that these
responsibilities can sometimes impact

emotional needs. All conversations
and responses will be treated

announcements.title: P.T.F.A: Pre-Loved School Uniform Sales
announcements.content: A quick reminder that our PTFA sells high-quality pre-loved school uniform through their Facebook page. It is a great way to save money, support the school, and give uniform items a new life. Extra items for the autumn term are available online.

announcements.title: Abbey College ASCA Music: In-School Instrumental & Vocal Tuition
announcements.content: Abbey College Music Service (ASCA Music) is providing in-school instrumental and vocal tuition this term at Warboys Primary Academy for Piano, Guitar, Drums, Violin, Woodwind, and Singing with qualified, DBS-checked tutors. Parents can register expressions of interest online.

announcements.title: Y.D.P Cambridge: Weekend Football Sessions at One Leisure Ramsey
announcements.content: Y.D.P Cambridge runs Sunday football coaching sessions at One Leisure Ramsey catering to all abilities. First session is FREE (£5 cash per session thereafter). Diddy's (ages 2–5): 10:00 AM – 11:00 AM; Little Legends (ages 6–11): 11:00 AM – 12:00 PM.

announcements.title: Ramsey Heritage Open Day (Sunday 13th September 2026)
announcements.content: Ramsey Heritage Open Day takes place on Sunday 13th September 2026 from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Features Sealed Knot, Vikings, and Roman re-enactors on Abbey Green. Free bus service from Ramsey Library to each historic site; free admission and parking.

announcements.title: 1st Warboys Scouts: Beavers, Cubs & Scouts Weekly Meetings
announcements.content: 1st Warboys Scouts welcomes new members to their weekly sessions: Beavers (ages 6 to 8) meet Tuesdays 6:00 – 7:00 PM; Cubs (ages 8 to 10.5) meet Tuesdays 6:30 – 8:00 PM; Scouts (ages 10.5 to 14) meet Wednesdays 7:00 – 8:30 PM.

Winter Fuel Payment recipients soar by 9.6 million after major Government U-turn
metadata.contentSnippet: Winter Fuel Payment recipients soared by 9.6 million to 10.9 million in England and Wales last winter after the Government widened eligibility.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Winter Fuel Payment recipients soar by 9.6 million after major Government U-turn
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The number of pensioners receiving the Winter Fuel Payment has soared by 9.6 million in just one year, new figures reveal, after the Government dramatically widened eligibility for the cash. Some 10.9 million people in England and Wales received the payment in winter 2025 to 2026, according to new Department for Work and Pensions statistics. That is a huge increase from the 1.3 million who received the payment in the previous winter. The latest figure is also around 290,000 higher than the 10.6 million recipients recorded in winter 2023 to 2024, when the payment was universal for most pensioners. The dramatic rise follows a major change to the rules. In winter 2024 to 2025, the Government restricted the Winter Fuel Payment to pensioners receiving certain means-tested benefits. But for winter 2025 to 2026, most pensioners living in England and Wales once again became eligible, provided they met the qualifying criteria. Those born on or before September 21, 1959 were eligible, although pensioners with income above £35,000 had their payment recovered by HMRC through the tax system. The DWP figures do not include subsequent HMRC recoveries and exclude pensioners who opted out of receiving the payment before it was made. The number of beneficiaries was even higher once eligible pension-age partners were taken into account. There were 11 million Winter Fuel Payment beneficiaries in winter 2025 to 2026. The payment was worth between £100 and £300, depending on the recipient's circumstances. Of all recipients: The majority of recipients were under 80, with 7.7 million people – 70 per cent – falling into this age group. Despite the much wider eligibility, 53,000 pensioners opted out of receiving their Winter Fuel Payment last winter. The Government's income-based recovery system also meant that some higher-income pensioners could receive the payment before HMRC reclaimed it. An HMRC impact assessment estimated that 2.2 million pensioners, including those in Northern Ireland, would be affected by these recoveries. The DWP said its latest statistics only cover payments made by the department and do not include money subsequently recovered by HMRC. The new figures also reveal a stark regional breakdown. North Yorkshire had the highest number of Winter Fuel Payment recipients, with 150,000, followed by Birmingham and Cornwall, both with around 140,000. At the other end of the scale, the Isles of Scilly had just 500 recipients, followed by the City of London with 1,200 and Rutland with 10,100. Recommended reading: The figures cover people living in England and Wales. Winter Fuel Payment has now been devolved to Scotland, which operates its own Winter Heating Benefit. The Winter Fuel Payment was introduced in 1997 to help pension-age people with their heating bills. It is an annual tax-free payment designed to help with the cost of heating a home during the winter. The latest figures provide the clearest indication yet of the scale of the Government's decision to reverse the sharp restriction in eligibility introduced the previous year.

metadata.title: New petition calls on council to cancel car park regeneration plans
metadata.contentSnippet: A new petition addressed to Huntingdonshire District Council calls for car-park regeneration plans to be scrapped.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: New petition calls on council to cancel car park regeneration plans
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. A new petition calls for Huntingdonshire's car-park regeneration plans to be scrapped. The proposals by property developer Capital & Centric involve the redevelopment of council-owned car parks in St Ives, Huntingdon and St Neots. At a full council meeting on September 9, councillors unanimously backed a motion to examine spending on the project. No planning application has been submitted, yet more than £1 million has already been spent on consultation. David Keane, district councillor for Hemingford Grey & Houghton, launched the petition to end the regeneration plans. He said: "We further ask Cabinet to confirm that these Council-owned sites will not be progressed for redevelopment under the current Capital & Centric programme, and that any future proposals for their use should only be considered through a new transparent process supported by a clear business case and meaningful engagement with residents, businesses and other affected stakeholders." Cllr Alex Bulat, district councillor for St Ives South, also backs the petition. Cllr Keane said the same request was being submitted through Huntingdonshire District Council’s official petition process, which can take 90 days. Cllr Keane said: "If HDC accepts and opens the official petition, we will publish the link and encourage supporters to sign that petition too." Earlier consultation plans included turning Princes Street Car Park and Huntingdon Bus Station into a housing development in Huntingdon. The proposals have also previously led Green councillors to leave the Liberal Democrat-led coalition on Huntingdonshire District Council, citing the council's handling of the regeneration plans.

metadata.title: St Neots prostate screening event could set world record with 122 men tested
metadata.contentSnippet: A prostate cancer awareness event in St Neots could set a new world record for the most men tested in a single day.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: St Neots prostate screening event could set world record with 122 men tested
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A prostate cancer awareness event in St Neots could set a new world record for the most men tested in a single day. The event, held at Eaton Socon Health Centre, saw 122 men screened by a team from North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust, led by surgeon Jyoti Shah MBE. Miss Shah said: "Prostate cancer is a silent killer, but it is a cancer that we can cure if we pick it up early enough. "It is the most common cancer in men in the UK, with one in eight being diagnosed at some point in their lives – and for men of Afro-Caribbean heritage, the risk is one in four." PSA blood tests were provided during the community event (Image: NHS) Campaigner Dave Young and the St Neots Prostate Cancer Support Group organised the event with support from Purple Horizons, attracting around 100 men. An application has been submitted to Guinness World Records to verify the achievement. Miss Shah praised Mr Young and the team for their efforts. She said: "The campaign was an enormous success and huge kudos to Dave Young and Purple Horizons for organising such a well-attended event. "I am so very proud of and grateful to my team for their dedication and giving their time to support this important community event – and to our Hospitals’ Charity for meeting the cost of the PSA tests." The PSA blood tests, funded by the North West Anglia Hospitals' Charity, typically cost £3.50 each. The awareness campaign was held at Eaton Socon Health Centre (Image: NHS) A handful of men have already been identified as needing a GP referral or hospital appointment. St Neots Town Councillor Sarah Pitt, who attended the event, spoke about the importance of raising awareness within the transgender community. Cllr Pitt said: "By speaking openly about having a PSA test, I hope I can encourage more people who still have a prostate, including trans women, to find out about PSA testing and consider whether it is appropriate for them." The current registered Guinness World Records mark is 258 men signed up for testing in eight hours, set in Egypt in 2024. Patients were due to receive their results directly, with their GPs notified and follow-up information provided where needed.

metadata.title: Community sustainability and supply chain champions invited to enter awards
metadata.contentSnippet: Entries are open for the Community Champion of the Year and the Supply Chain Business of the Year awards at the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Community sustainability and supply chain champions invited to enter awards
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Organisations, businesses and individuals making a positive environmental impact are being encouraged to enter two prestigious categories in this year's East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027. The Community Champion of the Year award celebrates those driving sustainability initiatives at a local level, while the Supply Chain Business of the Year award recognises organisations embedding environmental responsibility throughout their operations. Together, the awards shine a spotlight on the people and businesses leading the way in innovation, collaboration and sustainable change, while delivering measurable benefits for communities and the environment. COMMUNITY CHAMPION OF THE YEAR The Community Champion of the Year award recognises individuals, groups and organisations making a lasting difference through local sustainability initiatives. This category celebrates those who are leading environmental change in their communities through action, innovation and engagement. From grassroots projects and educational programmes to large-scale environmental initiatives, the award highlights efforts that deliver measurable benefits while inspiring others to get involved. Judges will be looking for nominees who have made an exceptional contribution to sustainability at a local level. Entries should demonstrate clear community impact, showing how work has improved environmental outcomes and created lasting change. Leadership and initiative will also play an important role. Entrants should show how they have driven projects forward, encouraged participation and championed sustainability within their communities. Evidence of collaboration with residents, schools, businesses, voluntary groups or public bodies will strengthen an application. Judges want to see innovative approaches to environmental challenges alongside measurable outcomes that demonstrate the value of the work undertaken. Last year’s award was won by PSH Environmental. The Rackheath-based recycling and waste management company was recognised for its community engagement and environmental initiatives. Reflecting on the win, managing director Nigel Parker said: “It’s really good to win this award. It’s a lot of hard work and effort and a case of doing the job properly!” CRITERIA The judges will be looking for an individual, group or organisation that has made an exceptional contribution to sustainability within their community. The winner should demonstrate leadership, innovation and a commitment to creating positive environmental change at the local level. The ability to inspire and engage others in sustainability efforts will be a key factor. The Supply Chain Business of the Year award celebrates organisations that are reducing environmental impact through sustainable supply chain management, innovation and collaboration (Image: Getty Images) SUPPLY CHAIN BUSINESS OF THE YEAR The Supply Chain Business of the Year award recognises organisations that are driving sustainability throughout their supply chains and demonstrating how environmental responsibility can go hand in hand with commercial success. This category highlights those taking meaningful action across sourcing, logistics, operations and supplier relationships. Judges will be looking for organisations that have successfully integrated sustainable practices across their supply chains while continuing to innovate and grow. Entries should show how environmental considerations influence decision making and operational processes, from procurement through to delivery. Strong applications should demonstrate the use of new technologies, systems or working practices that reduce environmental impact while improving efficiency. Collaboration with suppliers, partners and other stakeholders will also play an important role in the judging process. The award also recognises businesses that can demonstrate long-term impact. Judges will want to see measurable improvements in sustainability performance, together with evidence that their approach can be scaled or replicated elsewhere. Last year’s winner was Beccles-based Radical Waste, a waste management company recognised for integrating sustainability throughout its operations. The business was praised for its zero-waste model, investment in technology and broader environmental initiatives. Reflecting on the award, managing director Julian Knights said: “It’s game changing for us and an absolute honour and privilege to be awarded Supply Chain Business of the Year.” CRITERIA The judges will be seeking a company or initiative that has successfully integrated sustainability into its supply chain. Innovation, collaboration with partners and the long-term impact of the changes made will be key. The scalability of the model and measurable improvements in sustainability will also be assessed. Submit your entries before the deadline, which is midnight on Sunday, November 8. To enter the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027, please visit cleanandgreenawards.co.uk To find out more about all categories, please click here.

metadata.title: Recognising the businesspeople making a positive difference
metadata.contentSnippet: Find out what the Apprentice of the Year and Behaviour Change Campaign of the Year judges will be looking for at the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Recognising the businesspeople making a positive difference
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The East Anglia Clean & Green Awards are back! For this edition of the awards, innovation is the top priority, and both the Apprentice of the Year and Behaviour Change Campaign of the Year awards will celebrate businesses and individuals who are making an impact on sustainability in their sector. Here, the judges for these two awards tell us more about what they will be looking for from entrants. Elizabeth Conboy, executive director, commercial, RenewableUK, which sponsors Apprentice of the Year (Image: RenewableUK) Sponsored by RenewableUK Sponsor judge: Elizabeth Conboy, executive director, commercial, RenewableUK What do you bring to the judging process? I work closely with organisations across the renewable energy supply chain, from developers and manufacturers to technology providers and SMEs. That gives me a broad perspective on the skills, behaviours and leadership qualities that help individuals and businesses succeed in a fast-growing sector. Have you ever been judged for an award yourself? Yes, both personally and through the organisations I’ve been involved with. I understand the effort that goes into preparing an entry and how important recognition can be for individuals and teams. How will you use that experience when judging this award? I’ll look beyond polished submissions and focus on the substance of the achievement. Having been through the process myself, I understand the importance of giving every entry fair consideration and recognising different forms of success and impact. What will you be looking for in the winner? I’ll be looking for evidence of impact, a commitment to learning, and a genuine contribution to their organisation or the wider sector. I’m particularly interested in individuals who demonstrate initiative, collaboration and a desire to make a positive difference. What advice would you give to anyone that’s considering entering? Be authentic and don’t underestimate your achievements. Focus on the difference you’ve made, the challenges you’ve overcome and the lessons you’ve learned. The strongest entries clearly demonstrate impact and bring the individual’s story to life. Why is innovation an important judging consideration for this award? Whether it’s finding new ways of working, solving challenges or improving processes, innovative thinking helps organisations stay competitive and accelerates progress towards our net zero ambitions. Adam Tucker, account manager, Clarksons Port Services, which sponsors Behaviour Change Campaign of the Year (Image: Clarksons Port Services) Sponsored by Clarksons Port Services Sponsor judge: Adam Tucker, account manager, Clarksons Port Services Why were you keen to get involved in the Clean & Green Awards? I was keen to get involved in the Clean & Green Awards because they celebrate the organisations and individuals who are making a genuine difference to sustainability across our region. The campaigns recognised by these awards demonstrate how effective communication, collaboration and innovation can inspire people to make more sustainable choices and create lasting environmental impact. The awards are also an opportunity to celebrate success, share best practice and learn from one another. What do you bring to the judging process? In my role at Clarksons Port Services, I work closely with clients across offshore wind and the wider energy sector, giving me insight into the diverse approaches organisations are taking to support the energy transition. I’ll be looking at entries from both a commercial and practical perspective, recognising campaigns that have not only been creative but have also delivered measurable outcomes and genuine value for the audiences they were designed to influence. What will you be looking for in the winner? For me, the winning campaign will be one that can clearly demonstrate it has changed behaviours, not simply raised awareness. I’ll be looking for strong evidence of impact, supported by a creative, audience-focused approach that has inspired people to take meaningful, lasting action. What advice would you give to anyone that’s considering entering? I’d definitely encourage anyone who’s considering entering to do it. Don’t assume your campaign isn’t significant enough or that someone else has achieved more. If you’ve made a positive difference and can demonstrate the impact you’ve had, it’s worth sharing your story. Having been both an award entrant and a judge, I know that authenticity goes a long way. You don’t need to overcomplicate your submission; be honest, provide clear evidence and let the impact of your campaign speak for itself. Why should creative or innovative behavioural change strategies be celebrated? Behaviour change is rarely straightforward, which is why creative and innovative approaches deserve to be recognised. The most successful campaigns find new ways to connect with people, challenge established habits and make sustainable choices easier, more relevant and more achievable. The deadline for entries to the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards is Sunday, November 8 at midnight. For more information or to enter, please visit cleanandgreenawards.co.uk

metadata.title: Disgraced ex-Cambs copper to be sentenced over 'toxic' Whatsapp culture
metadata.contentSnippet: Disgraced celebrity police officer Paul Street, who created a “toxic” WhatsApp culture, will be sentenced later for misconduct in a public office.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Disgraced ex-Cambs copper to be sentenced over 'toxic' Whatsapp culture
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A disgraced celebrity police officer from Cambridgeshire who created a “toxic” WhatsApp culture will be sentenced later for misconduct in a public office. Ex-police sergeant Paul Street, 41, found fame in television crime shows on the BBC and Channel 4 and was known for getting “impressive results” through his “robust” style. However, anti-corruption officers began investigating him and uncovered his two WhatsApp groups in 2021 after a new police officer reported him. He encouraged colleagues to “bully” a teenage detainee and asked a workmate to send him a sex video of a female suspect, the Old Bailey had heard. The offences were committed while working at Cambridgeshire Constabulary leading a unit at Cambourne Police Station, mainly dealing with county lines drug supply and organised crime. Following an Old Bailey trial in June, Street, of Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, was found guilty of two charges of misconduct in a public office. Street had previously admitted two offences of unlawful disclosure of personal data relating to information and screenshots he sent to his partner in 2020. He will be sentenced alongside Josh Williams, 38, from Huntingdon, who pleaded guilty to misconduct in public office. The pair will appear at the Old Bailey before Judge Mark Lucraft KC on Wednesday morning. Eleven other officers were investigated over their conduct arising from the “toxic” culture Street had fostered. Of those, two resigned, one was dismissed for gross misconduct, one received a final warning, two received written warnings, and five others were dealt with for low level performance issues. During the trial, prosecutor Anne Whyte KC had described how Street “created a culture of bragging and intolerance towards suspects”, and a “zero-tolerance attitude to anyone on his team who disagreed with his methods and sentiments”. She had said: “He was not just promoting inappropriate attitudes, he was positively creating a toxic culture which junior officers would find difficult to challenge and likely to adopt.” In April 2020, Street called on his team to “bully” 17-year-old detainee Robiul Islam, encouraging them to “please hit him” and “smash his head in”. In the autumn of 2020, Williams was tasked with examining the phone of a female suspect he told Street was “quite fit”. Street asked him if there were “any nudes”, and Williams replied there was a video of the woman committing a sexual act. Williams went on to send Street a photo from the woman’s phone depicting her in underwear. The following year, Street asked on WhatsApp if Williams still had the intimate private video because he wanted to show it to “the lads from footy”. When he was interviewed about it, Street claimed he wanted to see the images to reassure himself the woman, who was released without charge, was not the victim of exploitative behaviour. But jurors were told it was not Williams’s job to discuss or share the private images, and neither was it Street’s job to ask for nudes or the sex video. Giving evidence, Street admitted his messages on WhatsApp were “poor” but said the language was “gallows humour” and part of the culture at the time. He also told jurors that being successful in his job had made him “arrogant”. Street had previously appeared on BBC show Britain’s Teenage Drug Runners in 2017, and in 2019 was on Channel 4’s Famous And Fighting Crime documentary. The prosecution asserted Street was more than a “maverick” officer with unorthodox methods and having good arrest rates did not justify his “out of control” behaviour.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Boys arrested after 14-year-old taken to hospital with knife injury
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Two boys have been arrested after a 14-year-old was taken to hospital with a knife injury. Emergency services were called to Orton Goldhay, Peterborough, at around 4pm yesterday (Monday September 14) with reports of a 14-year-old boy with a knife injury. A police cordon was put in place on playing fields next to Ormiston Bushfield Academy. Police and ambulance attended and the victim was taken to Peterborough City Hospital for treatment. Two 14-year-old boys from Peterborough have been arrested in connection with the incident. One boy remains in custody after being arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm, possession of a knife and theft. The other teenager was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm and assisting an offender. He has been bailed until December 14.

metadata.title: New 20-year Hunts parking plan set for debate as demand set to rise
metadata.contentSnippet: A new long-term parking strategy could soon shape the future of car parks and town centres across Huntingdonshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: New 20-year Hunts parking plan set for debate as demand set to rise
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Huntingdonshire District Council's cabinet is set to discuss a new 20-year parking strategy aimed at supporting town centres, improving customer experience and planning for future growth. Huntingdonshire District Council’s cabinet will consider the proposed plan when it meets today (Tuesday September 15). Work on the new parking strategy began in early October 2025 after a procurement exercise. The strategy will run from 2026 to 2046 and focus on economic growth, customer service and future demand. Read more Man arrested after young boy thrown into crocodile pit has bail extended Electric car charging stations could replace spaces at Hunts car park Six arrested after 'violent disorder' which seriously injured two men School council creates banner urging safer parking outside Hunts primary school Discover stunning National Trust site with 'something for everyone' The strategy will not set parking charges but will guide future decisions on tariffs and management. It outlines a vision for a "well-managed, balanced and future-focused parking service" that supports economic growth while promoting integration with public transport, walking, cycling, and electric vehicle infrastructure. The strategy has four aims: supporting thriving town centres, delivering a modern service, linking parking to sustainable transport and managing its assets responsibly. The council runs 25 off-street car parks with 3,149 spaces, according to evidence gathered for the strategy. Capacity is generally sufficient, but some town-centre car parks come under pressure at peak times. The council hired Ethos to study occupancy, assess parking and gather public views. The first survey drew 1,546 responses and the second drew 1,472. The second consultation found that 72 per cent backed the overall vision, while 95 per cent supported its focus on town centres and economic activity. The strategy warns that parking demand is expected to rise over the next two decades. By 2045, some car parks—particularly in Ramsey, Huntingdon and St Neots—could be under severe pressure, while others still have spare capacity. The plan proposes reviewing charges, stay limits and accessibility, improving signs and walking and cycling links, and adding more electric vehicle charging points. If approved, officers will draw up a phased plan, with some “quick win” measures expected within 12 to 18 months. The council said the first phase of engagement took place in December last year, before the second consultation sought views on the emerging vision, objectives and policy direction.

metadata.title: Inquest into death of Cambs killer Ian Huntley suspended pending murder trial
metadata.contentSnippet: An inquest into the death of Soham killer Ian Huntley will remain suspended pending the outcome of the murder trial of a fellow prisoner.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Inquest into death of Cambs killer Ian Huntley suspended pending murder trial
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An inquest into the death of Soham killer Ian Huntley remains suspended pending the outcome of the trial of a fellow prisoner charged with his murder. Huntley was allegedly attacked with a metal bar in a workshop at the maximum security Frankland Prison near Durham on February 26. Huntley was taken to the Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle, where he died on March 7. A brief inquest hearing in Crook, County Durham, was held where coroner Jeremy Chipperfield was told criminal proceedings had begun and a trial was due to start on November 23. Anthony Russell, 44, has been charged with murder and has appeared in court previously. Mr Chipperfield asked whether Russell had entered pleas and was told by his coroner’s officer that psychiatric assessments have been carried out on behalf of the prosecution and defence. The coroner said the inquest will remain suspended until the completion of the criminal proceedings and it will then be considered whether it was necessary to complete the inquest. Mr Chipperfield said: “That cannot happen until we know the shape of any trial.” He adjourned the inquest proceedings until December 16 for a further brief hearing. Huntley was serving a life sentence for the 2002 murders of 10-year-olds Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman. The ex-school caretaker killed the best friends after they left a family barbecue to buy sweets in Soham, Cambridgeshire, on August 4 2002. He dumped their bodies in a ditch 10 miles away. They were not found for 13 days despite a search involving hundreds of police officers. At the time, Huntley lived with Maxine Carr who was a teaching assistant at Holly and Jessica’s primary school. He denied murdering the girls but was convicted after a trial at the Old Bailey in 2003. He was jailed for life with a recommended minimum term of 40 years.

metadata.title: Cambs fraudster stole £40,000 from employer and spent it on skiing holiday
metadata.contentSnippet: A second-time fraudster from Ramsey has been jailed for stealing more than £40,000 from her employer and spending it on a skiing holiday.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambs fraudster stole £40,000 from employer and spent it on skiing holiday
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A second-time fraudster has been jailed for stealing more than £40,000 from her employer and spending it on a skiing holiday. Kirsty Payne, 44, of Taverners Drive, Ramsey, admitted defrauding her Cambridge-based employer, Marshall Thermo King, which trades as Marshall Fleet Solutions. In February 2025, she processed a £400,410 payment through the company system—£40,383 more than the legitimate amount. The extra funds were traced to an account belonging to one of Payne’s family members. The discrepancy went unnoticed until April, when Payne was signed off work because of her deteriorating mental health. During a wellbeing check with the company’s head of HR, she suddenly confessed to the fraud and resigned. She first claimed the money paid for a relative’s medical treatment, but later told police it funded a skiing holiday in the French Alps. Payne said the theft was a "spur of the moment" decision. However, she had a previous conviction for fraud by false representation and said she was experiencing financial difficulties despite earning around £80,000 a year. Payne told officers she had been struggling mentally, especially due to a family member’s terminal illness. But she could not explain why she took the money. Detective Constable Valentin Radulescu, who investigated the case, said: "Payne gave little thought to the impact of defrauding her employer out of tens of thousands of pounds. "By committing fraud for a second time she showed she had not learned her lesson, and this was looked on negatively by the courts, who imposed a custodial sentence which she had initially avoided. "I hope her time behind bars allows her to reflect on her actions and hopefully, this case also serves as a warning to anyone else hoping to turn a profit through deception." Payne pleaded guilty to fraud by false representation at Cambridge Magistrates’ Court in July. On September 10, she was sentenced to 18 months in prison at Peterborough Crown Court. The sentence included ten months for the latest fraud, plus extra time for breaching a suspended sentence for a previous similar offence.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Additional police presence after boy, 14, suffers knife injury near school
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: There will be an additional police presence in Peterborough today after a 14-year-old boy suffered a knife injury. The 14-year-old was injured in Orton Goldhay, Peterborough, at around 4pm on Monday, September 14. Emergency crews attended and police cordoned off playing fields beside Ormiston Bushfield Academy. The victim was taken to Peterborough City Hospital with serious but non-life-threatening injuries. Two 14-year-old boys from Peterborough have been arrested in connection with the incident. One remains in custody on suspicion of grievous bodily harm, possessing a knife and theft. The second was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm and assisting an offender before being bailed until December 14. Cambridgeshire Police said on the morning of September 15: "There will be an additional policing presence in the area today."

metadata.title: Project of the Year award seeks green initiatives with lasting impact
metadata.contentSnippet: Entries are open for the Project of the Year award, sponsored by Associated British Ports (ABP), at the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Project of the Year award seeks green initiatives with lasting impact
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Entries are now open for the Project of the Year award, sponsored by Associated British Ports (ABP), at the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027. This category celebrates initiatives that have delivered a significant positive impact and created lasting benefits. Paul Ager, divisional port manager, East Anglia at ABP, hopes to see projects that combine innovation with measurable results. “We’re looking for projects that deliver tangible environmental, social and economic benefits while demonstrating strong collaboration, innovation and long-term thinking,” said Mr Ager. “The strongest entries will show how they have addressed a real challenge, achieved measurable outcomes and created lasting value for their communities or industries.” He added that success in the awards can provide lasting benefits for entrants. “Recognition as a finalist or winner provides independent validation of the hard work, commitment and vision that goes into delivering a successful project,” he said. “The award also offers a platform to share best practice and inspire others.” Paul Ager, divisional port manager, East Anglia at ABP (Image: ABP) Innovation will be a key consideration during judging, reflecting the growing need for projects that can respond to changing environmental and economic challenges. Mr Ager said: “Innovation is often the difference between simply delivering a project and delivering one that creates lasting value. “As industries and communities continue to face new challenges, innovative thinking will be critical in delivering projects that support economic growth while advancing sustainability goals.” He believes the most successful projects are those that continue to generate benefits long after completion. “Success is not simply about delivering on time and on budget, although those factors are important,” said Mr Ager. “It is about creating value for customers, communities, stakeholders and future generations.” The entry deadline for the Project of the Year award is midnight on Sunday, November 8. For more information about the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027, please visit cleanandgreenawards.co.uk To read about all of the award categories, please click here. Associated British Ports (ABP) is the UK’s largest port operator. ABP’s ports collectively handle 25% of UK seaborne trade, worth £150bn+, and they play an important role in the energy transition as locations for renewable energy supply chains and generation. ABP contributes £15bn of gross value added to the UK economy, supports more than 200,000 jobs across the UK economy and provides jobs itself that are a third better paid than the UK average. Through fulfilling ABP’s twin missions of keeping Britain trading and enabling the energy transition, the company catalyses growth, prosperity and opportunity in coastal communities across Britain. The judges will be looking for a project that makes a substantial positive impact on the environment. Innovation, community involvement and scalability will be key factors. Entries should demonstrate measurable, long-term environmental benefits and serve as an example for future initiatives.

metadata.title: Teenager dies after car crashes into tree in Woburn street
metadata.contentSnippet: A teenager has died after a car left the road and crashed into a tree.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Teenager dies after car crashes into tree in Woburn street
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A teenager has died after a car left the road and crashed into a tree in Woburn. The crash happened on Sheep Lane at around 11pm on Sunday. The woman, who was in her late teens, was pronounced dead at the scene. Detective Constable Lotty Lewis of the Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire Roads Policing Unit said: "This was a tragic incident in which a young woman sadly died. "I would like to pay tribute to the emergency services who attended the incident and carried out extensive lifesaving efforts. "Any information may help us to establish what caused this incident to occur." Police believe other vehicles may have passed the crash scene and are asking drivers to check their dashcam footage. Anyone with information should report it at beds.police.uk/ro/report or call 101, quoting Operation Herring.

metadata.title: School statement after boys arrested and 14-year-old suffers knife injury
metadata.contentSnippet: Ormiston Bushfield Academy in Peterborough has spoken out after a teenager was injured with a knife and two boys were arrested.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: School statement after boys arrested and 14-year-old suffers knife injury
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Peterborough school has spoken out after a teenager was injured with a knife and two boys were arrested near its grounds. A 14-year-old boy suffered a knife injury during an incident in Orton Goldhay, Peterborough, at around 4pm on Monday September 14. Emergency services attended and police set up a cordon on playing fields next to Ormiston Bushfield Academy. The boy was taken to Peterborough City Hospital for treatment for serious but not life-threatening injuries. A spokesperson for the school said: "We are aware of an incident that took place outside school yesterday. "The safety and wellbeing of our entire school community is always our top priority and as soon as we became aware of this matter we took immediate action in line with our safeguarding processes and procedures. "We are also working with the authorities and providing support to any students, staff and families, as appropriate. "As an investigation is now underway, we are not able to comment further at this stage." Two 14-year-old boys from Peterborough have been arrested in connection with the incident. One remains in custody on suspicion of grievous bodily harm, possessing a knife and theft. The second was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm and assisting an offender. He has been bailed until December 14.

metadata.title: St Neots special school is making progress after being told it needed to improve
metadata.contentSnippet: St Neots special school Riverside Meadows Academy is making progress, according to a recent Ofsted monitoring visit.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: St Neots special school is making progress after being told it needed to improve
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Huntingdonshire special school previously found needing improvement by Government inspectors is making progress, according to a recent Ofsted monitoring visit. Riverside Meadows Academy in St Neots, a special school for pupils with social, emotional and mental health needs, was found to be taking "effective action" to address concerns raised in a previous inspection. The June 30, 2026 visit focused on leadership, teaching, the curriculum, attendance and behaviour. It followed a graded inspection in July 2025 that found the school to “require significant improvement”. Riverside Meadows Academy in St Neots is making progress in making improvements identified by an Ofsted inspection, according to the latest report by the Government watchdog. (Image: Google Maps/Street View) Ofsted inspectors said leaders and trustees are moving the school in the right direction after introducing a new senior leadership structure. The report said: "Leaders and trustees continue to move the school forward on its journey of improvement. "The trust has taken decisive action in establishing a new senior leadership structure to streamline its function and with clearly defined roles. Read more School council creates banner urging safer parking outside Hunts primary school Discover stunning National Trust site with 'something for everyone' Council submits planning application for landmark hub in Cambridgeshire town Pedestrian dies in crash involving bus on A14 St Ives theatre group prepares to stage charity performance "Leaders have had a positive impact in a short period of time on the areas of improvement identified at the last inspection." Staff were “positive about the work of leaders” and were “now working as a unified team across the two sites”. Curriculum planning, behaviour and attendance have all improved. Leaders have developed new curriculum pathways due to launch in September 2026 and are training staff to deliver them. The curriculum has been updated to better support the social, emotional and mental health needs set out in pupils’ Education, Health and Care (EHC) plans. The report said: "Leaders have made the most improvement in raising attendance and improving behaviours of pupils at risk of prolonged disengagement. "Since the last inspection, leaders have ensured that pupils are only accessing alternative provision most suitable to meet their needs." But inspectors said more work is needed, especially in reading and mathematics. The writing curriculum is clearly mapped out, but reading and mathematics lack the same level of detail. Ofsted said: "The reading and mathematics curriculum do not currently have the detailed knowledge pupils will need to know mapped out with the same clarity as seen in the writing curriculum. "The updated curriculum is not due to start until September 2026. "Therefore, it is not possible currently to see the impact of this change on pupils’ outcomes, including how well pupils achieve their EHC plan targets." Attendance is improving, but leaders are only beginning to analyse individual pupil data. Inspectors said more work is needed to extend the gains to more pupils. At the previous inspection, safeguarding was evaluated as being effective. The school has introduced a system to monitor pupils with high absence or repeated behavioural incidents. Targeted mentoring has sharply improved these pupils’ attendance, and the gains have been sustained. Suspensions have also decreased. The improvements are still at an early stage, but leaders plan to extend the approach to more pupils. Overall attendance and lesson engagement are improving. Inspectors said pupils were more engaged in class than at the previous monitoring visit. They credited the improvement to more consistent use of agreed teaching and behaviour strategies. Pupils also reported fewer instances of disruptive behaviour. Staff support also helped pupils manage assessments and exams more confidently. The section 8(2) monitoring inspection under the Education Act 2005 did not give the school new grades. Riverside Meadows Academy has 119 pupils and an executive headteacher overseeing both sites. Each site now has its own head of school and assistant headteacher. In 2021, then-headteacher Sarah Anderson–Rawlins received a Pearson Teaching Award for Excellence in Special Needs Education, while the academy also received a bronze Lockdown Hero Award.

metadata.title: St Neots Hockey Club men open season with two convincing wins
metadata.contentSnippet: St Neots Hockey Club’s men’s first and second teams opened their league campaigns with convincing wins.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: St Neots Hockey Club men open season with two convincing wins
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: St Neots Hockey Club’s men’s first and second teams opened their league campaigns with convincing wins. The first team travelled to Cambridge Nomads 1s and secured a 5-1 victory, putting last season’s disappointing campaign behind them. Andrew Pope, the second team’s top scorer last season, opened his account for the first team by scoring the only goal of the first half. Rory Jones doubled Saints’ lead early in the second half, finishing from a penalty corner. Nomads responded five minutes later by converting a penalty corner of their own. Saints restored their two-goal advantage through Bradley Forsdick, who scored the first of his second-half hat-trick. He added two more goals to complete the result, with one coming from a penalty corner and the other from open play. The second team began their promotion push with a 4-0 win over Bourne Deeping 3s. Saints had to wait 20 minutes for the opening goal, which was scored by Georgie Browne. They began the second half with more energy and quickly added two further goals. James Neuhauser scored one, while Mike Williams marked his debut with the other. Saints controlled the remainder of the half and completed the win in the final play, when Dan Wright struck a half-volley. Women's 1s after their loss to Bourne Deeping 1 (Image: St Neots Hockey) The women’s first team produced a good display in their opening match but lost 4-2 to Bourne Deeping 1s. Two quick goals put Saints on the back foot before Kira Herbert pulled one back late in the first half. Bourne scored again just before the interval. Herbert scored her second goal after the restart to reduce the deficit to one, but Saints could not find an equaliser. Bourne then scored on the counter-attack while Saints pushed for a leveller. The women’s second team worked hard in a goalless home draw against Cambridge South 4s. The men’s third team lost 5-0 away to City of Peterborough 7s. With the season under way, the club is seeking new players of all levels. Interested players can contact the club through social media or stneotshockeyclub.co.uk.

metadata.title: St Neots Under-18s score twice late to beat Harpenden 3-0 in FA Youth Cup replay
metadata.contentSnippet: St Neots Town Under-18s scored twice late on to beat Harpenden Under-18s 3-0 in the FA Youth Cup.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: St Neots Under-18s score twice late to beat Harpenden 3-0 in FA Youth Cup replay
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: St Neots Town Under-18s scored twice late on to beat Harpenden Under-18s 3-0 in the FA Youth Cup. The victory came in an extra-preliminary round replay after a closely fought first half. St Neots controlled more of the possession but struggled to break through Harpenden’s defence. The visitors looked dangerous when they counter-attacked, although they were unable to make clear progress against a well-organised home defence. The best chance before the interval fell to St Neots. Harpenden goalkeeper Joe Clarke made a good save to deny Ryan McCullogh, before diving bravely at the feet of Jack Noonan. The second half was more open, with St Neots taking control. They went ahead after 55 minutes when a ball over the visiting defence found substitute Philip Shampanov. He finished the chance to put the home side in front. Harpenden responded when Bobby Crisp was put clear of the St Neots defence, but goalkeeper Jayden Northrop saved at his feet. Northrop also made a good save from Murray Tyler as Harpenden tried to respond. St Neots continued to apply pressure. Noonan moved through the visiting defence before shooting just wide, then sent another effort over the bar after good work by Edward Yost. Clarke then made a good save from Shampanov, but Harpenden were forced back for much of the closing period. St Neots doubled their lead after 90 minutes when a Noonan shot was turned into the visiting goal by a Harpenden defender. The home side added a third goal in added time to complete the scoring and secure their place in the next round. St Neots’ starting team was Northrop, Southern, Smeathers, Egan, Pawlina, Keen, Noonan, Preidzius, Draper, McCullogh and Yost. Their substitutes were Nicholls, Lopez-Company, Setchell, Holman, Shampanov, Jemwa and Alessandro. Holman was shown a yellow card in the 83rd minute. Harpenden started with Clarke, McDonald, Smith, Efunbato, Crisp, Swaylam, Flack, Wilson, Murray-Bruce, Gower and Haggar. Their substitutes were Pearson, Tshehla, Foster, Pentland, O’Donovan, Davies and Woodley. Murray-Bruce received a yellow card in the 76th minute.

metadata.title: Godmanchester Rovers secure back-to-back wins after two comebacks
metadata.contentSnippet: Godmanchester Rovers secured back-to-back victories in three days, recovering from a difficult first half at Peterborough before defeating the joint league leaders.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Godmanchester Rovers secure back-to-back wins after two comebacks
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Godmanchester Rovers secured back-to-back victories in three days, recovering from a difficult first half at Peterborough before defeating the joint league leaders. The two United Counties Premier League Division South fixtures were played at FC Peterborough on Wednesday September 2 and at home against Atherstone Town on Saturday September 5. The midweek game began badly, with the home side controlling possession and taking a deserved lead through an unfortunate own goal. Jamie Short sliced a dangerous cross beyond goalkeeper Jack Mason, leaving Rovers trailing despite the visitors' attempts to contain Mohammed Mhamdi on the left. Mason then produced several saves to ensure the deficit remained one goal at half-time. Manager Seb Hayes' changes transformed the contest after the interval. Zane Campbell's run and cross allowed Matty Allan to equalise at the far post after 54 minutes. Five minutes later, Ed Randerson won a free-kick, and Andre Williams curled the set-piece into the net to complete the comeback. Jamie Mastropierro, Ethan Moffat-Gibbs and Ben Tait helped the away side withstand late pressure. Back at home, Rovers faced joint leaders Atherstone and again survived a testing opening period. The visitors created the clearer chances, but Jamie Short cleared off the line and Mason dealt confidently with crosses into his area. He also saved with his legs after the restart as the home side began to impose itself. The breakthrough came in the 73rd minute when captain Craig Gillies chased a long ball, exploited defensive hesitation and lobbed the stranded goalkeeper. Atherstone threatened an equaliser, but the hosts sealed victory five minutes from time. Substitute Harry Biggs won possession near the corner, escaped two challenges on the goal line and crossed for Allan to finish. The result extends Rovers' strong run, while Callaghan remained absent under concussion protocols. They host in-form Desborough Town next.

Business owners in Cambridgeshire urged to review their fire safety measures
metadata.contentSnippet: Business owners in Cambridgeshire are being urged to review their fire safety measures during a month-long workplace fire prevention campaign

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Business owners in Cambridgeshire urged to review their fire safety measures
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Business owners across Cambridgeshire are being urged to review their fire safety measures during a month-long workplace fire prevention campaign. Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service is using September to remind businesses to update their fire risk assessments and meet their duties under the Fire Safety Order. The service has also produced short animated videos explaining common fire safety problems found during inspections. Topics covered include checks on fire doors, emergency lighting and fire alarm systems, as well as general guidance on fire risk assessments and fire safety legislation. Station Commander Leon Collins, from the service's Fire Protection team, said: "We know that business owners have a lot on their plates and fire safety is often not at the top of the to-do list. "So, we want to help make it easier to access the information they need and make it more engaging than reading a guidance document, which is why we have added to our series of short animated videos." Campaign - Business owners are being reminded to check their fire safety measures (Image: Essex Fire) He said the videos focus on areas that inspectors frequently identify when visiting businesses. Mr Collins added: "We've added useful videos about some of the common things that our inspectors see when they visit companies, such as when to check fire doors, emergency lighting and fire alarm panels. "These go with the other videos that provide a basic introduction to Fire Risk Assessment and the Fire Safety Order." As part of the campaign, fire officers will also host a Fire Safety Presentation at Cambridge Fire Station on September 24 at 2pm. The session, which can also be attended online, is aimed at helping business owners and managers better understand their legal responsibilities and the measures needed to keep workplaces safe. Mr Collins said: "Attending a session will provide a better appreciation of the Fire Safety Order, the need for assessment of fire risk and the application of fire safety measures within the workplace. "We really encourage business owners to book a place at a presentation as it provides a useful introduction to workplace fire safety, whatever level of experience you might have." Further information about the presentations and the fire safety videos is available through the Business Safety section of the fire service website.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire farmers call for national food targets as UK self-sufficiency falls
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire farmers are calling for national targets to increase homegrown food production and strengthen food security.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire farmers call for national food targets as UK self-sufficiency falls
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire farmers are calling for national targets to increase homegrown food production and strengthen food security. The call came on Wednesday, September 9, during Back British Farming Day, as National Farmers’ Union research showed Britain is producing less food than 30 years ago. NFU Cambridgeshire chair Alison Morris, who farms near March, said: "Back British Farming Day is a great opportunity to champion our industry, highlight our concerns and thank the public for their amazing support. "Farming is crucial to Cambridgeshire, with farmers here driving the economy, caring for our countryside, and supporting the environment, all while working to world-leading animal welfare standards as we feed the nation and strive to deliver national food security." Farmers met Paul Bristow, mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, and deputy mayor Anna Bailey at a farm near Ely to discuss food security. The NFU’s Ready to Grow report says the UK has become less self-sufficient in 10 of 11 staple foods, including wheat, vegetables, beef, poultry and eggs. Food imports have risen by 70 per cent, while exports have barely grown. Ms Morris said: "The government needs to take national food security seriously and setting ambitious targets for homegrown food production would be an important step forward in helping us to achieve this. "We thank the mayor and deputy mayor for meeting with us to give us the opportunity to raise our concerns." The public backs the NFU’s call, with a OnePoll survey finding that 93 per cent of British households support maintaining or increasing UK food self-sufficiency. The report also highlights pressure on farmers from drought, disease outbreaks and rising costs. The NFU has also called for legislation to ensure the UK's food self-sufficiency does not fall below its current level of 60 per cent.

metadata.title: New sustainable businesses invited to enter One to Watch Award
metadata.contentSnippet: Entries are open for the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027 One to Watch Award, celebrating sustainable new businesses. Enter by November 8.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: New sustainable businesses invited to enter One to Watch Award
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027 are open for entries, including the the One to Watch Award, sponsored by Pier. This category shines a light on outstanding new East Anglian businesses which demonstrate commercial viability while contributing to environmental sustainability. Amy Bendall, managing director of award sponsor Pier, said: “There is always appetite for innovation, but organisations working to make a difference simply with the resources they have and the right attitude to responsible business, is just as important.” She said she’d love to hear from new organisations across sectors who are ready for more people to learn about what they do and their approach to operating with green-thinking. Amy Bendall, managing director of Pier (Image: Pier Marketing Limited) “East Anglia has long been at the heart of the renewables revolution,” she added. “But, there is an opportunity to champion our green credentials too, particularly as we face a changing and challenging climate. “Sustainable thinking has to be essential for businesses and organisations going forward – these awards are a fantastic opportunity to help inspire others to do better, and do more.” Mrs Bendall said stand-out businesses will be ones that have a “point to prove” – whether that’s driving sustainability solutions or operating as sustainably as they can. “We all have the power to make a difference. New businesses can do so much to drive that momentum with fresh thinking, which is what makes ‘One to Watch’ such an exciting category.” She said it’s often newer businesses that understand the balance between success and environmental impact. Mrs Bendall added: “The two could and should go hand-in-hand, and it’s something that makes ‘One to Watch’ a really important award category.” At Pier, the team often advises clients to enter awards. She explained: “It’s a door to greater visibility and recognition with people who could make a real difference to the success of your organisation.” Submit your entries before the deadline, which is midnight on Sunday, November 8. To enter the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027, please visit cleanandgreenawards.co.uk To find out more about all categories, please click here. Pier is an award-winning integrated communications agency, which was established in Felixstowe in 2008 by Kate Bowden Smith. From PR and campaigns to community consultation and stakeholder engagement, the agency delivers strategic communications for clients locally, nationally and globally. For more than a decade, Pier has been at the forefront of the renewables revolution, supporting wind, solar and battery developers, supply chain businesses and organisations across the wider sector. Beyond renewables, Pier helps organisations turn their sustainability ambitions into credible campaigns that make an impact. As a proud Suffolk business with sustainability at its heart, Pier is pleased to be part of the Clean & Green Awards, celebrating positive environmental change. The judges in this category will be looking for a business which is less than five years old and can demonstrate strong commercial viability. Its core activity must contribute positively to environmental sustainability in some way. Innovation and differentiation, traction and progress, and leadership and vision will also need to be demonstrated by the winning business.

metadata.title: Equipment worth £100,000 stolen in Hunts golf club break-in
metadata.contentSnippet: Golfing equipment worth more than £100,000 has been stolen from a club on Needingworth Road in St Ives.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Equipment worth £100,000 stolen in Hunts golf club break-in
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Equipment worth more than £100,000 has been stolen from a Huntingdonshire golf club. Police were called to the club on Needingworth Road, St Ives, just after 10.30pm on Friday, September 11. A gate and glass doors were smashed during the break-in and golfing equipment believed to be worth more than £100,000 was stolen. No arrests have been made and investigations are ongoing. Cambridgeshire Police want to hear from anyone who saw suspicious activity or has dashcam, doorbell or CCTV footage. They are particularly keen to hear from anyone who saw a Land Rover near the club before or after the break-in. Anyone with information should contact police online or call 101, quoting reference 35/70616/26. Information can also be given anonymously to Crimestoppers.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Police close Hunts home after drug use and anti-social behaviour
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Huntingdonshire home linked to repeated anti-social behaviour and drug use has been partially closed by police. The property, 33 Drovers Pace, in Huntingdon, became the subject of a closure order following reports of drug use and anti-social behaviour. Cambridge Magistrates’ Court issued the order on Friday, September 11, following an application from Cambridgeshire Constabulary’s Huntingdon Neighbourhood Team. PC James Ferries, from the team, said: "Residents living in the surrounding area have endured no end of anti-social behaviour. "The closure order allows the tenant to remain living at the address but will prevent those attending to commit anti-social behaviour and other criminal offences." Until December 11, only the tenant, Places for People and emergency services can enter the property. The order was made under the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014.

metadata.title: Charity auction raises more than £3,000 for local causes
metadata.contentSnippet: A black-tie charity auction involving two care homes, The Chase in Huntingdon and Henbrook House in St Neots, raised more than £3,000 to support veterans and people facing homelessness.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Charity auction raises more than £3,000 for local causes
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Residents and staff from two Huntingdonshire care homes raised more than £3,000 for charities supporting veterans and people facing homelessness. A black-tie auction organised by Connaught Care involved two of its homes, The Chase in Huntingdon and Henbrook House in St Neots. The event was held in support of SSAFA, the Armed Forces charity, and 3 Pillars, which supports people facing homelessness. The charity auction raised more than £3,000 for good causes (Image: The Chase and Henbrook House) Lauren Mair, general manager at The Chase, said: "When we started planning the charity auction, it felt important to us that the residents have a clear say in where the money should go. "Many people here have seen first-hand how homelessness can affect communities, and we also have many residents with strong family connections to the Armed Forces. "Supporting those causes therefore felt like a natural choice, and we’re so proud to have raised such a substantial amount." The fundraiser, held at The Chase, featured auction lots including pamper sessions, afternoon teas, weekend breaks, large-screen TVs, artwork and wine. Residents, families and members of the wider community attended. Both charities were selected by residents and address issues that are closely linked, as housing insecurity is a known concern for some former members of the Armed Forces. Government data shows that veterans who are homeless or living in temporary accommodation are less likely to feel prepared for civilian life than those who own their homes. Veterans experiencing homelessness also tend to delay seeking help and can face barriers engaging with mainstream support services. Michael Zinaka, general manager at Henbrook House, said: "It was fantastic to bring The Chase and Henbrook House together for an evening like this. "Seeing residents, families and local people come together to get behind the same effort was truly heartwarming. Proceeds from the event were donated to chosen charities (Image: The Chase and Henbrook House) "Working together meant we could make the evening bigger, reach more people and give something meaningful back to the communities around us. metadata.title: Hunts council chairman defends handling of debate after clash at meeting
metadata.contentSnippet: The chairman of Huntingdonshire District Council has defended his handling of a debate during a controversial council meeting.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Hunts council chairman defends handling of debate after clash at meeting
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Huntingdonshire council chairman has defended his handling of a debate during a controversial council meeting. Cllr Stephen Ferguson, chairman of Huntingdonshire District Council, clashed with Cllr Ryan Coogan at a full council meeting on Wednesday, September 9. The issue arose during a debate over a motion to conduct a review into funds for the Capital & Centric proposals to build housing developments on three popular car parks. Cllr Coogan, the Reform councillor for Yaxley, objected after an amendment cut his motion from four pages to two. The pair clashed after Cllr Ferguson ordered Cllr Coogan to stop speaking and sit down, but he refused. Councillors Ryan Coogan and Stephen Ferguson clashed at a meeting last week (Image: HDC) In a statement on social media, Cllr Ferguson said he wanted to explain his actions after “discussion online”. He said: "The member concerned had already spoken three times during the debate, more than any other member. "At no point was I seeking to prevent them from speaking or expressing their views." He said the speech had strayed from the motion, breaching a council rule on debate. Councillor Ferguson said: "I first tried, from the Chair, to remind the member to speak to the motion, an intervention which would have taken a few seconds. "He simply continued speaking over me." Cllr Ferguson said he stood during the debate, meaning the meeting had to fall silent, but Cllr Coogan continued speaking over him. He then adjourned the meeting. Councillor Ferguson said: "I then resumed the meeting, returned to the Chair and, importantly, gave him the opportunity to continue his speech. "These are the same rules I had applied throughout the evening, and the same basic principles I have applied over many years of chairing councils at every level of local government. "They are there to ensure that debate is orderly, relevant and fair, and I will continue to apply them impartially." Cllr Coogan hit back on social media, claiming Cllr Ferguson had stopped him from “exposing the truth”. The amendment at the heart of the controversy was passed at the meeting by 28 votes to 18. The council then unanimously backed the motion to review spending on the car-park plans. The proposals had already led to the collapse of Huntingdonshire District Council's joint administration, after Green councillors quit the Liberal Democrat-led coalition over its handling of the regeneration plans.

metadata.title: Six arrested after 'violent disorder' which seriously injured two men
metadata.contentSnippet: Six people have been arrested after violent disorder on The Broadway, in St Ives, which left two men with serious injuries.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary:
Six people have been arrested after violent disorder in a Huntingdonshire town which left two men with serious injuries. Police received multiple calls to The Broadway, in St Ives, on the evening of August 29 reporting violence and criminal damage in the town centre. Two men were taken to hospital where they were treated for serious but not life threatening injuries. Two 19-year-old men, from Hartford and St Ives, have been arrested on suspicion of a public order offence. A 20-year-old man from Huntingdon has been arrested on suspicion of a public order offence and possession of drugs. A 29-year-old woman from Wyton has also arrested on suspicion of a public order offence. Read more Men injured and car damaged after fight in Huntingdonshire town
    Photos capture aftermath of fight in Huntingdonshire town as two arrested
    Ten people jailed across Cambridgeshire this month for crimes from rape to arson
    Woman arrested after 'distraction burglary' in Huntingdonshire town
    Progress update on £329m A141 and St Ives transport scheme Meanwhile, a 19-year-old man from Whittlesey was arrested on suspicion of assault occasioning grievous bodily harm. They have all been bailed pending further enquiries and further arrests are expected in the coming weeks, Cambridgeshire Police confirmed. A sixth person, a man from Chatteris, was arrested on suspicion of a public order offence but has since been released without charge. Detective Inspector Luke Pedlar said: "Violence and disorder of this nature has no place in our communities and we know this incident will have caused concern among residents, businesses and visitors in St Ives. "Our investigation has progressed quickly and we have already made a number of arrests, with further enquiries ongoing. "We are committed to identifying everyone involved and ensuring they are held accountable for their actions. "I would like to thank the community for their support so far and continue to urge anyone with information, footage or who witnessed the disorder to come forward and speak to us." metadata.contentSnippet: Plans have been submitted to install an electric vehicle charging hub at King James Retail Centre in Godmanchester, near Huntingdon.
